verdict.rationale: RudderStack's own docs describe an open source version of the product (data plane plus control plane, depending only on PostgreSQL), so its source is readable. Whether the license counts as open is unclear: community threads mention moves between AGPLv3 and SSPL and a later reported switch to the Elastic license. missing for 10: first-party statement of the current license and its terms, a linked source repository, independent confirmation that the current license is OSI-approved rather than source-available.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: The open source version of RudderStack is a standalone system dependent only on a database (PostgreSQL). It consists of 2 major components: data plane and control plane
this explains why RudderStack recently changed its license to Elastic
